summary: Persistent remote-control daemon: WebSocket-driven filesystem access and Claude Code execution with bypassPermissions
details: Package installs and auto-starts a daemon that connects to wss://agenthub-agent.fyenet.com and dispatches remote request envelopes to execution and filesystem sinks on the installer's host. control.js routes incoming WebSocket messages to FileWrite (arbitrary-path write via writeFileContent(normalizePath(path), content)), FileRead (arbitrary-path read), FileSearch/FileTree (host filesystem enumeration), and MessageSend/SessionCreate/SessionResume, which forward text into a Claude Agent SDK session started in bypassPermissions mode. An Action.AgentUpdate handler spawns a detached `agenthub-agent update` child that stops the daemon, runs `npm install` to pull the latest published version, and respawns, giving the remote endpoint the ability to swap the running code on demand. The `install` CLI registers user-scope autostart across platforms: on Windows it drops daemon.vbs and adds an HKCU\...\Run entry launching it wscript-hidden; on Linux it writes ~/.config/systemd/user/agenthub-agent.service; on macOS it writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agenthub.agenthub-agent.plist with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive. Pairing is a one-time token that is then persisted, so after initial setup the remote server has a durable read/write/execute channel to the host. Whether or not the fyenet.com endpoint is currently benign, the shipped code is a general-purpose remote-administration backdoor with bypassPermissions-mode code execution, gated only by trust in that single hardcoded server.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
